content: We need number of carbonyl (C=O) groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of molecule. We can use IR spectra to detect C=O stretch, or carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-210 ppm). Use IR spectra tool (cheapest?). Both carbon NMR and IR are single measurement. Probably IR is cheaper? Both cost similar. Use IR to see if carbonyl present and count peaks? Might be ambiguous. Carbon NMR could show carbonyl signals; each carbonyl carbon gives a distinct peak. Use carbon_nmr_spectra to get list of chemical shifts. Then count peaks in carbonyl region (190-220 ppm). Let's do carbon NMR.
